report.report:
# MachineSense report — normal__20.2752

Research demonstration; development results; not validated for real machines.

## Verdict
**healthy — caution: a healthy-baseline check disagrees; consider a recheck**. Decision rule: provisional research setting: The decision rule is a provisional setting, not a final rule selection; the final choice will be made later under stated assumptions about fault frequency and costs.

The classifier's top class is normal and both of its checks passed.
Caution (b1s disagrees): a healthy-baseline check disagrees; consider a recheck.
Narrowly above the speed-aware baseline (B1s) threshold (+0.063 %).

## Checks against the calibrated thresholds
- Classifier confidence (MSP) 0.999940 ≥ 0.998895: pass (margin +0.001045, +94.544 % on the 1 − MSP scale).
- Familiarity (Mahalanobis distance) 13.87 ≤ 30.04: pass (margin -16.17, -53.828 %).
- Autoencoder error 0.089754 ≤ 0.243072: within healthy limit (margin -0.1533, -63.075 %).
- Speed-aware baseline (B1s) 0.872695 > 0.872143: above healthy limit — caution (margin +0.0005513, +0.063 %).

3 of 4 alternative decision rules agree with the rule in use (the difference comes from a narrow margin).

## Most probable classes (CNN-6 scores)
- normal > 0.9999, imbalance < 0.0001, horizontal misalignment < 0.0001
- Secondary logistic regression's top class: normal
- Model scores are not the probability that the diagnosis is correct.

## Signal quality
- Measured shaft speed 19.82 Hz (1189 rpm); speed stable within the recording (0.27 %).
- No signal-quality warnings.

## Bearing frequencies at the measured speed
BPFO 59.4 Hz, BPFI 99.1 Hz, BSF 37.1 Hz, BSF DEFECT LINE 2X 74.2 Hz, FTF 7.4 Hz.

## Secondary logistic-regression evidence
These are feature contributions of the secondary logistic-regression model; they explain that model, not the main neural network's decision. Top features for normal:
- largest |sample| in the window (underhang tangential) [f_under_tangential_peak]: contribution +1.068
- RMS of the window (DC removed) (underhang tangential) [f_under_tangential_rms]: contribution +0.866
- excess kurtosis (Fisher) of the window (overhang radial) [f_over_radial_kurtosis]: contribution +0.682
- amplitude at 1× the window's shaft speed (overhang tangential) [f_over_tangential_o1]: contribution +0.670
- largest |sample| in the window (overhang radial) [f_over_radial_peak]: contribution +0.610

## Limitations
- Research demonstration; development results; not validated for real machines.
- Calibrated on 5 healthy recordings; trained on speeds below 40 Hz and on the development pool only.
- Decision rule is a provisional research setting, not a final rule selection.
- The tested scores and rules do not consistently distinguish the imbalance / vertical-misalignment pair when one class is withheld. The classifier distinguishes them well when both are represented in training. This does not establish that no representation, training objective or decision method could help.
- Predicted fault location is according to the dataset labels; the classifier does not independently verify the physical sensor mapping. Per-channel reconstruction error is not fault-location evidence.
- Reserved-test eligibility: this bundle may be used for the final Q1 (healthy vs fault), Q2 (closed-set known condition) and severity / speed-block extrapolation tests, since no reserved recording was used; it is NOT eligible for the Q3 leave-one-class-out evaluation, because it was trained on all ten classes.

method.statistic: 95th percentile of max(ratio, 1/ratio) over the pairs

channels.method: mean over the 9 windows of R1 features (ml.features.recording_features), compared with the healthy training recording nearest in measured speed; a channel is marked only if a metric's change factor max(ratio, 1/ratio) exceeds the typical healthy variation of that channel and metric (95th percentile over pairs of training normals within ±3 Hz); volt metrics need at least one side ≥ 0.005 V; excess kurtosis is not ratioed; at most 2 channels, the furthest beyond their band
